'''Synaptic''' is a [[GTK]]-based [[graphical user interface]] designed for the [[APT (software)|APT]] [[package manager]] used by the [[Debian]] [[Linux distribution]] and its derivatives.<ref name = "Garcia, ubunlog, 2013" /> Synaptic is usually used on systems based on [[Deb (file format)|deb]] packages but can also be used on systems based on [[RPM Package Manager|RPM]] packages. It can be used to install, remove and upgrade software packages and to add [[Software repository|repositories]].

==Usage==
Synaptic is a lightweight package manager that enables the user to install, upgrade or remove software packages.<ref name="FOSSAP">{{cite web |last1=Prakash |first1=Abhishek |title=Using the Lightweight Package Manager Synaptic in Ubuntu Linux |url=https://itsfoss.com/synaptic-package-manager/ |website=It's Foss |date=4 March 2024 |access-date=26 September 2025 |ref=FOSSAP}}</ref> To install or remove a package a user must search or navigate to the package, then mark it for installation or removal. Changes are not applied instantly; the user must first mark all changes and then apply them.<ref name="MUODD">{{cite web |last1=Delony |first1=David |title=How to Graphically Manage Packages on a Chromebook With Synaptic |url=https://www.makeuseof.com/chromebook-manage-packages-graphically-with-synaptic/ |website=Make Use Of |date=2 March 2023 |access-date=26 September 2025 |ref=MUODD}}</ref><ref name="MUOSH">{{cite web |last1=Hameed |first1=Sharqa |title=How to Install Synaptic Package Manager on Ubuntu |url=https://www.makeuseof.com/install-synaptic-package-manager-on-ubuntu/ |website=Make Use Of |date=17 October 2023 |access-date=26 September 2025 |ref=MUOSH}}</ref>

==History==
Synaptic development was funded by the Brazilian company [[Mandriva#History|Conectiva]],<ref name = "Softpedia, 2007" /> which asked Alfredo Kojima, then an employee, to write a graphical front-end for APT, continuing the work initiated with the creation of the APT RPM back-end, [[apt-rpm]].
